title: Fewest Train Hops
statement: A rail network has n towns, numbered 0 to n − 1. Each line in `lines` runs between two towns in both directions, and every ride along one line counts as one hop. Return the fewest hops from town `from` to town `to`, or −1 if there is no way.

answerKey.pattern: Breadth-first search for the shortest path in an unweighted graph
keyPoints: Build an adjacency list with both directions
BFS from `from` with a distance array, −1 meaning not reached
Set a town's distance when it is added to the queue, one more than the town it came from
The distance of `to` when BFS ends (or when it is reached) is the answer
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Repeatedly relax every line until distances stop changing: O(V · E)

hints: Every hop costs the same. Which search reaches towns in order of their number of hops?
Breadth-first search: all towns 1 hop away, then 2 hops away, and so on.
Keep a distance array filled with −1. When a town is added to the queue, its distance is the current town's distance plus 1.
